Ashoka. The third emperor of the Mauryan Empire initially conquered aggressively, but the bloodshed at Kalinga around two hundred sixty BCE—killing an estimated hundred thousand and enslaving many more—horrified him into spiritual conversion to Buddhism. He issued edicts promoting dharma, vegetarianism, animal welfare, and religious tolerance across the empire. Ashoka sent Buddhist missionaries throughout Asia via the Silk Road, widely credited with transforming Buddhism into a major world religion and building approximately eighty-four thousand stupas.
